events.headline: Jaxson Dart undergoes season-ending knee surgery; Jameis Winston is the Giants starter
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 22 item. Dart had season-ending surgery Wednesday and the Giants formally placed him on injured reserve Thursday; the damage includes the MCL, PCL and meniscus, with no ACL involvement. Jameis Winston was already named the starter going forward, beginning Week 3 at home against Tennessee. Malik Nabers' right shoulder popped out in the same Monday night loss to the Rams; he popped it back in and returned, and no further diagnosis has been reported. On Wednesday the Giants listed Nabers as limited with the shoulder (an estimated report, since they held a walkthrough), with no quotes on his status.
events.so_what: No longer a planning question: Dart is done for 2026 and the Giants' rushing-QB premium goes with him. Winston throws more and riskier balls, which can mean more volume for Nabers and the other pass catchers alongside more drive-ending interceptions (only a point each here). Nabers being limited rather than out on the first report is a mild positive; watch Friday's designation before locking him in.

events.headline: Bears' Thursday report: Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent, Kyle Monangai and Cairo Santos all DNP; Case Keenum the only healthy QB
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 23 item. Chicago did not practice Thursday, so the report was an estimate: Williams (hamstring) and Bagent (concussion protocol) would not have practiced, leaving Case Keenum as the only healthy quarterback on the 53-man roster, with Miller Moss on the practice squad and likely to be elevated. Running back Kyle Monangai (knee) and kicker Cairo Santos (right hip) were also listed as non-participants, and the Bears have no backup kicker on the roster. Ben Johnson has said Williams won't practice this week but has not ruled him out for Monday night against Philadelphia.
events.so_what: Plan the Monday game around Keenum. A Williams start would be a late surprise after most lineups lock, and every Bears pass catcher is a downgrade either way. Monangai's knee is new: if he sits, D'Andre Swift's share of the backfield grows. Santos's hip puts the Bears kicker in doubt too, and a kicker who can't score by the distance bands is a sit.

events.detail: Brooks hurt his groin in the Week 2 win over Atlanta, will have core muscle surgery and is out at least six games on injured reserve. events.so_what: Brooks moves to an IR slot where one exists and is off the radar until at least midseason. Hubbard's hold on the early downs and goal line strengthens with no 1B behind him, unless Carolina revisits Ekeler.

events.headline: Falcons name Michael Penix Jr. the Week 3 starter vs. Green Bay after Cooper Rush struggles
events.detail: The Falcons announced Monday that Penix starts Thursday night against the Packers, his first start since a season-ending knee injury last November. Cooper Rush started the first two games, both losses, completing 56.4% of his passes with one touchdown and four interceptions. Tua Tagovailoa was a full practice participant Tuesday for the first time since his Sept. 10 oblique injury and is listed as Penix's backup.
events.so_what: A quarterback change on a short week after Rush threw four interceptions in two games (an interception costs only a point here, but each one still ends a drive). Penix's first game back off a knee reconstruction is a real risk, and a healthy Tagovailoa behind him shortens his leash, so treat him as a streaming option, not a lock. The Thursday game means a lineup decision by Wednesday.

events.so_what: Not a fantasy starter on his current production, so this mainly matters as a depth note at a shallow position.

events.headline: Chargers send tight ends David Njoku (fibula) and Charlie Kolar (forearm) toward IR; Oronde Gadsden is the lone TE
events.detail: Jim Harbaugh said both tight ends are headed to injured reserve after getting hurt against the Raiders, Njoku with a fibula injury and Kolar with a forearm injury, which means a minimum of four games each. That leaves Oronde Gadsden as the only tight end on the active roster; Harbaugh said he has "a lot of confidence" in him and that the team is working with personnel on adding another. One later NBC Sports roundup says Kolar may avoid IR after surgery; unverified against the team's own account.
events.so_what: Gadsden inherits every tight-end snap in a Mike McDaniel offense for at least a month, and at a position this shallow a full-time role is the whole case. He is a streaming answer for any roster short a TE with Njoku out, and a legitimate FLEX consideration only if the target share follows the snaps.
